formats.platform: TradingView Strategy Tester: List of trades CSV (every header generation seen 2021 to Sep 2026)
formats.export_name: Strategy Tester > 'List of trades' tab > Download/Export button. Saves a .csv. Real filenames look like '<Strategy_name>_<EXCHANGE>_<SYMBOL>_<YYYY-MM-DD>[_<5hex>].csv' (e.g. 'P6_Strategy_CME_MINI_MNQ1!_2026-09-05.csv'). Older builds used '<Strategy>_List_of_Trades_<YYYY-MM-DD>[_<5hex>].csv'. Each Strategy Report tab downloads separately; only this tab contains trades.
formats.file_type: csv (comma-delimited; '.' decimal; no thousands separator; UTF-8. Since about late 2025 the file starts with a UTF-8 BOM)
formats.structure:
One header row, then TWO rows per trade number: an entry row and an exit row. Trade-level values (P&L, excursions, cumulative, duration) are REPEATED on both rows. Locate the file by stripping the BOM and checking that the first header cell is 'Trade #' or 'Trade number' and the second is 'Type' (German: 'Typ').

Header generations, verbatim from real exports:
G1 legacy (files 2021 to Feb 2025): Trade #,Type,Signal,Date/Time,Price USD,Contracts,Profit USD,Profit %,Cum. Profit USD,Cum. Profit %,Run-up USD,Run-up %,Drawdown USD,Drawdown %
  Type values: 'Entry Long','Exit Long','Entry Short','Exit Short' (capitalised side). Trades run newest first (descending Trade #), and within a trade the Exit row comes BEFORE the Entry row. Run-up and Drawdown are positive magnitudes.
  A 2022 variant has 'Price' with no currency and 'Profit NONE','Cum. Profit NONE','Run-up NONE','Drawdown NONE' when the strategy currency is NONE; that variant runs ascending with the Entry row first.
G2a (files ending Oct to Dec 2025): Trade #,Type,Date/Time,Signal,Price USD,Position size (qty),Position size (value),Net P&L USD,Net P&L %,Run-up USD,Run-up %,Drawdown USD,Drawdown %,Cumulative P&L USD,Cumulative P&L %
  Type values are lowercase: 'Entry long','Exit long','Entry short','Exit short'. Rows ascend by trade number with the Exit row first. Drawdown is NEGATIVE.
G2b (seen 2026-03): Trade #,Type,Date and time,Signal,Price USD,Position size (qty),Position size (value),Net P&L USD,Net P&L %,Favorable excursion USD,Favorable excursion %,Adverse excursion USD,Adverse excursion %,Cumulative P&L USD,Cumulative P&L %
G2c (seen 2026-04 and 2026-05): same as G2b but with 'Size (qty)','Size (value)'.
G3a (seen 2026-05-28): Trade number,Type,Date and time,Signal,Price USD,Size (qty),Size (value),Net PnL USD,Net PnL %,Favorable excursion USD,Favorable excursion %,Adverse excursion USD,Adverse excursion %,Cumulative PnL USD,Cumulative PnL %
G3b (current; seen 2026-07 to 2026-09-05): Trade number,Type,Date and time,Signal,Price USD,Size (qty),Size (value),Net PnL USD,Return %,Commission USD,Favorable excursion USD,Favorable excursion %,Adverse excursion USD,Adverse excursion %,Cumulative PnL USD,Cumulative PnL %,Duration (bars)

Currency suffixes: the Price column carries the symbol's quote currency ('Price USD', 'Price USDT'). Money columns carry the strategy/account currency, which can differ: a real file has 'Price USD' next to 'Net PnL GBP', 'Commission GBP' and 'Cumulative PnL GBP'. Match headers with a regex on the prefix and capture the trailing currency code.

LOCALISATION: headers and Type values follow the TradingView UI language. Verified German header: Trade #,Typ,Datum und Uhrzeit,Signal,Preis USD,Größe (Menge),Größe (Wert),G&V netto USD,G&V netto %,Positive Exkursion USD,Positive Exkursion %,Negative Exkursion USD,Negative Exkursion %,Kumulativer G&V USD,Kumulativer G&V %. German types are 'Long-Einstieg','Long-Ausstieg','Short-Einstieg','Short-Ausstieg', and the open-trade signal is 'Offen'.
Spanish headers could NOT be verified, and the Spanish-speaking target market is exactly where they matter. Column order is the same across locales, so: (a) keep a per-language alias table, (b) fall back to matching by position when the column count equals a known generation (14/15/17) and the first column is an integer trade number, and (c) tell the client in the upload UI to switch TradingView to English before exporting.

Other rules:
- 'Size (value)' / 'Position size (value)' = entry price x qty x point value, and it is the same on both rows (verified on MES: 7591.25 x 1 x 5 = 37956.25).
- 'Return %' / 'Net P&L %' = net P&L / Size(value) x 100.
- 'Cumulative ... %' = cumulative P&L / initial capital x 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
- Percent columns are in percent units (3.53 means 3.53%).
- Partial exits and pyramiding produce SEPARATE trade numbers that share an entry or exit timestamp. A real fixture has 440 rows = 220 TV 'trades' but only 130 positions.
columns: Type (Entry long/Exit long/Entry short/Exit short; legacy capitalised Entry Long...; de: Long-Einstieg/Long-Ausstieg)
Signal (entry/exit order id or comment; exit row of an open trade = 'Open' / de 'Offen')
Profit % | Net P&L % | Net PnL % | Return %
Cum. Profit <CCY> | Cumulative P&L <CCY> | Cumulative PnL <CCY>
Cum. Profit % | Cumulative P&L % | Cumulative PnL %
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
1. Group rows by the trade-number column. Each group should hold exactly 2 rows; flag any other count as malformed. Row order differs by generation (descending and exit-first in G1, ascending and exit-first in G2/G3, entry-first in 2022 files), so classify rows only by Type: entry if Type starts with 'Entry' (case-insensitive) or ends with '-Einstieg'; exit if it starts with 'Exit' or ends with '-Ausstieg'.
2. Side = long/short, read from the Type token.
3. qty = the Contracts/Size (qty) value, which is unsigned and the same on both rows.
4. entry_time and entry_price come from the entry row; exit_time and exit_price come from the exit row.
5. pnl_net = the Profit/Net P&L/Net PnL value in account currency (read it from the exit row). TradingView reports NET of the commission configured in strategy properties (verified: 0.0128 x (1618.65 - 1560.29) = 0.747 gross, minus 0.1%/side = 0.71 as reported).
6. Commission: in G3b, commission = the 'Commission <CCY>' column, which is MEASURED, and gross = net + commission. In other generations per-trade commission is NOT_MEASURED; the commission rate can be DECLARED from the XLSX Properties sheet ('Commission' value, unit not stated).
7. MFE and MAE come from Run-up/Drawdown or Favorable/Adverse excursion. Sign convention: legacy G1 drawdown is positive; G2+ adverse is negative. Normalise to abs().
8. OPEN trade: the exit row's Signal is 'Open' ('Offen' in German). Its Date/Price are the last bar close and its P&L is unrealised. Exclude it from closed trades and report it as an open position.
9. Do NOT merge partial exits or pyramid legs into one position by default; that changes the trade count TradingView reports. Optionally derive 'positions' by grouping legs that share entry timestamp + entry signal and summing qty and pnl.
10. Timestamps carry no timezone. They are in the chart timezone (exchange timezone by default), so tag the timezone NOT_MEASURED or DECLARED by the client.
11. Date format is usually 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'. Real files also show 'DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM' (UK locale, likely re-saved from Excel, with CRLF endings) and ISO 8601 with offset. Detect day-first vs month-first across the whole column; if still ambiguous, refuse and ask.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
Only closed-trade (realised) equity can be measured from the file.
1. Sort closed trades by exit_time, then by trade number.
2. equity_t = initial_capital + cumsum(pnl_net). Aggregate trades that close at the same timestamp (partial exits and pyramid legs share an exit time).
3. Cross-check against the 'Cumulative P&L/PnL' column. It accumulates in trade-number order, and its value on the last closed trade should equal sum(pnl_net) within 0.01 x n_trades. A mismatch is a red flag (edited file).
4. initial_capital is not in the CSV. Take it from the XLSX Properties sheet 'Initial capital', or DECLARED by the client. It can be roughly inferred as cum / (cum% / 100); that estimate is imprecise because cum% is rounded to 2 decimals, so tag it as derived.
5. The Favorable/Adverse excursion columns give a per-trade intratrade worst case. Use them to show that closed-trade drawdown understates the true drawdown. Intrabar equity is NOT_MEASURED in the CSV; the XLSX 'Max equity drawdown (intrabar)' can be shown as DECLARED.

formats.encoding_notes:
- Strip the BOM (open with utf-8-sig).
- Accept CRLF or LF.
- A Signal containing a comma is quoted.
- An empty Signal is possible on the exit row.
- Numbers never use thousands separators in genuine exports; if one appears, the file was re-saved by Excel, and its dates may be reformatted too.
- tradingview.com, backtestbase.com and mylinedchart.com were blocked by the egress proxy during this research. Every layout above was confirmed from real exports committed to public GitHub repos, dated by their filenames.

formats.platform: TradingView Strategy Tester: full report XLSX
formats.export_name: Strategy report header: strategy name dropdown (or the report's '...' menu) > 'Download data as XLSX' / 'Export data'. Produces one .xlsx workbook with every report tab.
formats.file_type: xlsx (Office Open XML). Reading it needs openpyxl, which the repo does not currently install; add it as an optional extra, or parse xl/workbook.xml, xl/sharedStrings.xml and xl/worksheets/sheetN.xml with zipfile + xml.etree from the stdlib.
formats.structure:
Sheets, verbatim and in order, from a real May 2026 export: 'Performance', 'Trades analysis', 'Risk-adjusted performance', 'List of trades', 'Properties'. Sheet names are localised (German: 'Liste der Trades').

'List of trades': row 1 is the header, identical to the CSV generation current at export time (e.g. Trade #,Type,Date and time,Signal,Price USDT,Size (qty),Size (value),Net P&L USDT,Net P&L %,Favorable excursion USDT,Favorable excursion %,Adverse excursion USDT,Adverse excursion %,Cumulative P&L USDT,Cumulative P&L %). Unlike the CSV:
- 'Date and time' cells are Excel serial date NUMBERS with a date style (e.g. 44952.375 = 2023-01-26 09:00), in the chart timezone.
- Numeric cells are typed numbers.
- Percent cells are numbers in percent units.

'Performance', 'Trades analysis' and 'Risk-adjusted performance': row 1 = ['', 'All <CCY>', 'All %', 'Long <CCY>', 'Long %', 'Short <CCY>', 'Short %']. Metric names are in column A:
- Performance: Initial capital, Open P&L, Net profit, Gross profit, Gross loss, Expected payoff, Commission paid, Buy & hold return, Buy & hold % gain, Strategy outperformance, Max contracts held, Annualized return (CAGR), Return on initial capital, Account size required, Return on account size required, Avg margin used, Max margin used, Margin efficiency, Avg equity run-up duration (close-to-close), Avg equity run-up (close-to-close), Max equity run-up (close-to-close), Max equity run-up (intrabar), Max equity run-up as % of initial capital (intrabar), Avg equity drawdown duration (close-to-close), Avg equity drawdown (close-to-close), Return of max equity drawdown, Max equity drawdown (close-to-close), Max equity drawdown (intrabar), Max equity drawdown as % of initial capital (intrabar), Net profit as % of largest loss, Largest winner as % of gross profit, Largest loser as % of gross loss.
- Trades analysis: Total open trades, Total trades, Winning trades, Losing trades, Even trades, Percent profitable, Avg P&L, Avg winning trade, Avg losing trade, Ratio avg win / avg loss, Largest winning trade, Largest winning trade percent, Largest losing trade, Largest losing trade percent, Outliers, Outliers P&L, Avg # bars in trades, Avg # bars in winning trades, Avg # bars in losing trades.
- Risk-adjusted performance: Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, Profit factor, Margin calls.

'Properties': header ['name','value'], then Trading range, Backtesting range, Symbol, Timeframe, Point value, Chart type, Currency, Tick size, Precision, <every script input by its display name>, Initial capital, Order size, Pyramiding ('0 orders'), Commission (bare number such as '0.1'; the unit/type is not stated), Slippage ('0 ticks'), Verify price for limit orders, Margin for long positions, Margin for short positions, Recalculate after order is filled, Recalculate on every tick, Recalculate on bar close, 'Backtesting precision. Use bar magnifier'.
columns: List of trades: same columns as the CSV generation current at export time
Performance/Trades analysis/Risk-adjusted performance: <metric>, All <CCY>, All %, Long <CCY>, Long %, Short <CCY>, Short %
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
Same pairing rules as the CSV, applied to the 'List of trades' sheet. Convert serial dates: datetime(1899,12,30) + timedelta(days=value).

The script inputs in 'Properties' give a free, verifiable parameter record. Count how many inputs exist as a hint for the declared-trials / DSR question; this is DECLARED, not a trial count.

The 'Commission', 'Slippage', 'Pyramiding' and 'Backtesting precision. Use bar magnifier' properties feed red flags: zero commission, zero slippage, and no bar magnifier with intrabar stops.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
1. equity = Properties 'Initial capital' + cumsum(net pnl) over closed trades sorted by exit time. The capital comes from the uploaded file, so tag it MEASURED-from-file.
2. Check that the final value equals initial capital + Performance 'Net profit' (All column) minus Open P&L.
3. Show Performance 'Max equity drawdown (intrabar)' and 'Sharpe ratio' as DECLARED, since they are TradingView's own numbers, and compare them with the engine's MEASURED values from the reconstructed curve.

formats.platform: cTrader (cTrader Algo / cBot backtesting): report.html with embedded JSON, and the --report-json file
formats.export_name:
Three routes lead to the same camelCase JSON:
- cTrader Desktop: Backtesting > save/export report (HTML). cTrader also writes 'report.html' and 'events.json' automatically into the cBot's data/.../Backtesting folder.
- cTrader CLI: 'ctrader-cli backtest ... --report=<file.html> --report-json=<file.json>'.
- The Plugin API BacktestingCompleted event exposes the same JSON report.
formats.file_type: html (JSON embedded in a <script> tag) or json
formats.structure:
Inside report.html, find <script type="application/json" id="backtesting-report">{...}</script> and json.loads its contents. The --report-json file is the same object without the HTML wrapper. The CLI's stdout summary is a different, PascalCase shape; do not accept it.

Top-level keys, verbatim: main, equity, tradeStatistics, parameters, usedSymbols, positions, orders, history, entries, profitsLosses, roi.

main: utcOffset (minutes, display only), language, depositAsset, depositAssetDigits, period ('h1'), symbol, brokerTitle, cBotName, roi, netProfit, startingCapital, endingEquity, endingBalance, testingPeriod{duration,startDate,endDate (epoch ms),formatted}, accountType ('hedging'|'netting'), accountLeverage, data{type e.g. 'tickDataFromServer', isCustom, customName}, spread, commissions{type e.g. 'usdPerMillionUsdVolume', value, applyCommissionAutomatically}, theme, titleKind ('backtesting'), authorNickName, authorLink, cBotLink, embedded.

equity: points[{balance, minEquity, maxEquity, timestamp (epoch ms)}], maxBalanceDrawdownPercent, maxEquityDrawdownPercent, maxBalanceDrawdownAbsolute, maxEquityDrawdownAbsolute.

history: {columns:[...], items:[...]}. 'columns' is only the user's visible grid column order (it varies between files); always read the item keys. Item keys: id, symbol, direction ('buy'|'sell'), net, gross, entryTime, closeTime (epoch ms UTC), entryPrice, closePrice, swaps, commissions (NEGATIVE = cost), volume (units), quantity (lots), label, comment, balance (balance after close; present in items even when it is not listed in columns), pips.

positions: {columns, items (still open at test end), marginUsed, freeMargin, marginLevel, unrealizedNet, unrealizedGross}. Position item keys: id, symbol, quantity, volume, direction, entryPrice, tp, sl, commissions, closingCommissions, created, label, comment, pips, net, gross, swaps.

orders: {columns, items}.

tradeStatistics: each metric is {all,long,short}. Metrics: netProfit, profitFactor, commissions, swaps, totalTrades, winningTrades, maxConsecutiveWinningTrades, largestWinningTrade, losingTrades, maxConsecutiveLosingTrades, largestLosingTrade, averageTrade.

parameters: [{group, displayName, propertyName, value}].

usedSymbols: [{symbol, period, baseAsset, quoteAsset, commissions, swapLong, swapShort, digits, lotSize, pipPosition, ...}].
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
Each history item is already one closed round trip: a position close, or one partial close with its own id.
- side: 'buy' = long, 'sell' = short.
- qty = volume (units); quantity is in lots.
- entry_time = entryTime and exit_time = closeTime. Both are epoch ms UTC, so the timezone is MEASURED.
- entry_price = entryPrice and exit_price = closePrice.
- pnl_net = net; gross = gross; commission = -commissions; swap = swaps.
- Identity net == gross + commissions + swaps held on all 115 real rows checked (tolerance 0.01). Fail the check if violated.
- Each item's balance equals the previous balance + net.
- positions.items are open at the end of the test: report them as open, never as closed.
- Cross-check count and sum against tradeStatistics.totalTrades.all and tradeStatistics.netProfit.all.
- main.data.type and main.commissions / main.spread feed cost red flags (e.g. commission value 0, or m1 bars instead of ticks).
formats.equity_reconstruction:
Best, and MEASURED: equity.points gives balance plus the minEquity/maxEquity envelope at irregular timestamps (about per bar or per change). That supports a real mark-to-market drawdown, which can be checked against maxEquityDrawdownAbsolute.
Fallback: main.startingCapital + cumsum(net) ordered by closeTime. This must match each item's balance and main.endingBalance.
formats.encoding_notes:
- The HTML is UTF-8. Extract the JSON with a non-greedy regex between 'id="backtesting-report">' and the next '</script>'. Never execute any script.
- Real reports also carry parameters, usedSymbols, entries, profitsLosses and roi. The parser must not require them; the minimal fixture above omits them.
- The CLI --report-json flag is known to crash with some cBots. In that case report.html is the reliable artifact.
- help.ctrader.com and community.ctrader.com were blocked by the egress proxy. The schema was confirmed by parsing 3 real report.html files from GitHub (2022 to 2026).

formats.platform: cTrader: History grid 'Export to Excel' (backtest History tab, and live trade statements)
formats.export_name: Backtesting results > History tab > right-click the grid > 'Export to Excel' (.xlsx). Live-account statements also export as .xlsx (sheet 'Records') or CSV (first line 'Deals').
formats.structure:
One row per closed position/deal. The first line of the CSV statement variant is the literal word 'Deals'; the header follows. Column headers verified from cTrader trade-statement exports that use the same grid:
- Real 2026 CSV: Deal ID,Order ID,Symbol,Opening Direction,Closing Direction,Opening time (UTC+8),Closing Time (UTC+8),Entry price,Closing price,Closing Quantity,Commissions,Pips,Net USD,Channel,Balance USD
- Real xlsx 'Records' sheet: ID, Symbol, Opening direction, Opening time, Closing time, Entry price, Closing price, Closing Quantity, Swap, Commission, Net $, Pips, Label, Comment
- Other variants seen in parsers: 'Opening time (UTC+0)', 'Swaps' (plural), 'Net (USD)', 'Net €', 'Balance €', 'Gross USD'.
The timezone is embedded in the header text, e.g. '(UTC+2)'. Capitalisation varies ('Opening Direction' vs 'Opening direction').

NOT verified on an actual backtest-grid export: headers may differ slightly from the statement export. Prefer report.html.
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
One row = one closed round trip.
- side: Opening direction 'Buy' = long, 'Sell' = short.
- qty: strip the ' Lots' suffix. The value is in lots, so units are unknown without the lot size; mark qty as lots.
- Times: parse with the UTC offset taken from the header (formats seen: '21 Aug 2026 02:38:02.095', 'DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS.fff', '10.07.2026 09:31:22').
- pnl_net = Net column. It already includes commissions and swaps, which are negative numbers.
- gross = Gross if present, else net - commissions - swap.
- Rows without a closing time are open positions.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
The 'Balance <CCY>' column is the running balance after each close, so the measured closed-trade equity is balance by closing time. Watch the formatting: thousands can use a space, as in '36 483.87'.
If no balance column: DECLARED starting capital + cumsum(Net).

- Thousands separator is a space (or a narrow no-break space) in Balance.

formats.export_name: Strategy Analyzer > select a backtest > display 'Trades' > right-click the grid > 'Export...' > CSV (Excel is also offered). The Trade Performance window's Trades grid exports the same way.
formats.file_type: csv (delimiter and decimal separator follow Windows regional settings: ',' with '.' in en-US; ';' with ',' in most EU locales)
formats.structure:
One header row, then one row per round trip. The header ends with a trailing delimiter, which produces an empty last column.
- NT 8.1.x, verified in 2025 and 2026 files: Trade number,Instrument,Account,Strategy,Market pos.,Qty,Entry price,Exit price,Entry time,Exit time,Entry name,Exit name,Profit,Cum. net profit,Commission,Clearing Fee,Exchange Fee,IP Fee,NFA Fee,MAE,MFE,ETD,Bars,
- Earlier builds and Trade Performance exports: Trade number,Instrument,Account,Strategy,Market pos.,Qty,Entry price,Exit price,Entry time,Exit time,Entry name,Exit name,Profit,Cum. net profit,Commission,MAE,MFE,ETD,Bars,

Account = 'Backtest' for Strategy Analyzer output. Instrument uses NT contract naming ('ES 12-25', 'MNQ MAR26').

Money cells follow the currency format: '$1244.92', negatives in parentheses '($455.08)'; an EU example is '-$ 200,00'. Dates follow the Windows culture: '1/26/2022 3:10:00 PM' in en-US, 'd/M/yyyy HH:mm:ss' in EU.

IMPORTANT: Profit, Cum. net profit, MAE, MFE and ETD follow the Strategy Analyzer 'Display unit' (Currency, Percent, Pips, Ticks or Points). Require Currency, and reject cells that are not money-formatted.

Headers are localised when the NinjaTrader UI language is not English. Spanish names seen in one third-party parser ('Instrumento', 'Precio de entrada', 'Tiempo de entrada', 'Ganancias', 'Comisión') are UNVERIFIED.
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
Already one row per round trip. When an exit partially fills or scales out, several rows share an entry time; keep them as separate trades.
- side: Market pos. 'Long'/'Short'.
- qty = Qty (contracts).
- Entry/exit time and price come straight from their columns.
- pnl_net = Profit. It is NET of commission and fees. Verified: ES short 25 pts x $50 = $1250 - $5.08 = $1244.92, and MNQ 20 x 0.75 x $2 = $30 - $38 = ($8.00).
- commission = Commission + Clearing Fee + Exchange Fee + IP Fee + NFA Fee (positive magnitudes); gross = Profit + commission.
- MAE and MFE are positive magnitudes in currency.
- ETD (end trade drawdown) = MFE - Profit. Use it as a consistency check.
- Bars = bars in trade.
- Tag costs MEASURED only when Commission is non-zero. Zero commission on futures is itself a red flag.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
Starting capital is NOT in the file, so it must be DECLARED.
1. equity = capital + 'Cum. net profit', taken at each Exit time.
2. Verify that Cum. net profit equals the running sum of Profit; a mismatch is a red flag.
3. Intratrade risk is available only from MAE. Mark-to-market equity is NOT_MEASURED.

formats.encoding_notes:
- Sniff the delimiter (',' vs ';').
- Parse money by stripping currency symbols, spaces and NBSP; '(x)' means negative.
- Infer the decimal separator per column. A lone separator followed by exactly 3 digits is a thousands separator.
- Dates: detect day-first vs month-first over the whole column; AM/PM is present in en-US.
- ninjatrader.com was blocked by the egress proxy. Headers were confirmed from real exports on GitHub (ES/MNQ/NQ, 2022 to 2026).

formats.export_name: Backtest results page > Trades tab > 'Download Trades'. Saves '<Backtest name>_trades.csv'. Timestamps are UTC.
formats.structure:
One header row, then one row per closed trade, as built by LEAN's TradeBuilder. Verbatim header, confirmed in 3 independent real files:
Entry Time,Symbols,Exit Time,Direction,Entry Price,Exit Price,Quantity,P&L,Fees,MAE,MFE,Drawdown,IsWin,Order Ids
- Times are ISO 8601 UTC with 'Z' ('2020-04-01T14:00:00Z').
- Symbols is always quoted and may contain spaces (options: "SPXW  190114P02460000").
- Direction is 'Buy' (long) or 'Sell' (short).
- Quantity is unsigned.
- P&L is GROSS (verified: 40 x (38.268 - 42.52) = -170.08).
- Fees is positive.
- MAE <= 0 and MFE >= 0, both in account currency.
- Drawdown = LEAN EndTradeDrawdown (profit given back, >= 0).
- IsWin is 0 or 1.
- Order Ids is a quoted list that starts with a TAB character ("\t5,6").
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
Already one row per round trip.
- side: Buy = long, Sell = short.
- qty = Quantity.
- Times: parse ISO 8601 as UTC; the timezone is MEASURED.
- pnl_gross = P&L; commission = Fees (MEASURED); pnl_net = P&L - Fees.
- Do NOT treat P&L as net; LEAN's Trade.ProfitLoss is documented as gross.
- Several symbols in one row mean a multi-leg trade. Keep it as one trade, and flag instrument = multi.
- IsWin can be used as a consistency check, but recompute wins from pnl_net.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
Start equity is not in the CSV. Take it as DECLARED, or read 'Start Equity' from the backtest result JSON (statistics['Start Equity'] or totalPerformance.portfolioStatistics.startEquity).
- From trades: equity = start + cumsum(P&L - Fees), by Exit Time.
- Preferred, when the client also uploads the result JSON: charts['Strategy Equity'].series['Equity'].values = [[unix_seconds, open, high, low, close], ...]. Older files use [{x,y}] points. This gives MEASURED mark-to-market equity.
formats.encoding_notes:
- Strip the leading TAB inside 'Order Ids'.
- Rows may end with a trailing space.
- The UI docs call the button 'Download Trades'. The quantconnect.com docs came from search snippets only; the header was confirmed from real committed files.

formats.platform: QuantConnect / LEAN: 'Download Orders' CSV and backtest result JSON
formats.export_name:
Orders: backtest results page > Orders tab > 'Download Orders' saves '<Backtest name>_orders.csv'.
Result JSON: LEAN CLI 'lean backtest' writes backtests/<timestamp>/<id>.json (plus <id>-summary.json and <id>-order-events.json); the same object comes from the QC API readBacktest.
formats.structure:
ORDERS CSV, verbatim header: Time,Symbol,Price,Quantity,Type,Status,Value,Tag
- Time is ISO 8601 UTC 'Z'.
- Quantity is signed (+ buy, - sell).
- Type examples: 'Market', 'Market On Open', 'Limit', 'Stop Market'.
- Status: 'Filled', etc.
- Value = Price x Quantity (signed).
- Tag is free text, quoted if it contains commas (e.g. 'Liquidated').
- Rows end with a trailing space.
- The file has NO fee column.

RESULT JSON (camelCase since about 2023; older files are PascalCase):
- top keys: rollingWindow, charts, orders, profitLoss, statistics, runtimeStatistics, state, algorithmConfiguration, totalPerformance, analysis.
- totalPerformance = {tradeStatistics, portfolioStatistics, closedTrades[]}.
- closedTrades item: id, symbols[{value,id,permtick}], entryTime, entryPrice, direction (0=Long, 1=Short), quantity, exitTime, exitPrice, profitLoss (gross), totalFees (positive), mae, mfe, duration ('2.00:00:00'), endTradeDrawdown, isWin, orderIds.
- orders: a dict keyed by order id, each {type (0=Market,...), id, symbol{value}, price, time, quantity (signed), status (3=Filled), direction (0=Buy, 1=Sell), value, tag, ...}.
- statistics: string-valued ('Start Equity', 'End Equity', 'Total Fees', 'Sharpe Ratio', 'Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio', ...).
- algorithmConfiguration: {accountCurrency, startDate, endDate, parameters, tradingDaysPerYear, ...}.
- charts['Strategy Equity'].series['Equity'].values = [[unix_s, o, h, l, c], ...].
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
ORDERS CSV:
1. Keep only Status == 'Filled'.
2. Pair per Symbol with FIFO lot matching. A position opens when the net position leaves 0 and closes when it returns to 0 or flips sign; split on a flip.
3. side = the sign of the opening Quantity.
4. pnl_gross = sum over matched lots of qty x (exit - entry) x sign.
5. Fees are NOT_MEASURED from this file alone.

JSON: use totalPerformance.closedTrades directly, with side from direction (0 long, 1 short), pnl_net = profitLoss - totalFees, and commission = totalFees (MEASURED).
formats.equity_reconstruction:
The JSON's 'Strategy Equity' series holds candle arrays of [unix_seconds, open, high, low, close] (daily or sampled). Use close as the equity level and low for intraperiod drawdown; both are MEASURED.
Start equity = statistics['Start Equity'].
From orders only: equity = DECLARED start + realised pnl_gross, which is costs-NOT_MEASURED.
formats.encoding_notes:
- Accept both camelCase and PascalCase JSON.
- The enums are integers: direction 0/1, order status 3 = Filled.
- Orders CSV fields may carry trailing whitespace.

formats.platform: backtesting.py (kernc): stats._trades and stats._equity_curve saved with pandas to_csv
formats.export_name: stats = Backtest(...).run(); stats._trades.to_csv('trades.csv'); stats._equity_curve.to_csv('equity.csv'). stats['_trades'] is the same object.
formats.file_type: csv (pandas default: leading unnamed RangeIndex column, ',' delimiter, '.' decimal)
formats.structure:
TRADES header by version, verified from source and real CSVs:
- v0.3.x (common in 2023 files): ,Size,EntryBar,ExitBar,EntryPrice,ExitPrice,PnL,ReturnPct,EntryTime,ExitTime,Duration
- v0.4.0 to 0.5.x: the same plus a trailing Tag column.
- v0.6.0 to 0.6.4: ,Size,EntryBar,ExitBar,EntryPrice,ExitPrice,SL,TP,PnL,ReturnPct,EntryTime,ExitTime,Duration,Tag, then indicator snapshot columns Entry_<name> / Exit_<name> (quoted when the name has commas, e.g. "Entry_SMA(C,10)"; a multi-line indicator adds _0, _1 suffixes).
- v0.6.5+ (2025-07-30): ,Size,EntryBar,ExitBar,EntryPrice,ExitPrice,SL,TP,PnL,Commission,ReturnPct,EntryTime,ExitTime,Duration,Tag + Entry_/Exit_ columns.
Duration is serialised as a pandas Timedelta string ('14 days', '0 days 04:00:00'). EntryTime/ExitTime are serialised as dates when every value is midnight ('2004-11-17'), otherwise as datetimes.

EQUITY header: <index name or empty>,Equity,DrawdownPct,DrawdownDuration. The index is usually named 'Date' or 'Datetime' when the OHLC frame had a named index. DrawdownDuration is only populated at drawdown ends.
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
Each row is a closed trade.
- side: long if Size > 0, short if Size < 0; qty = abs(Size) in units.
- entry and exit come from EntryTime/EntryPrice and ExitTime/ExitPrice. There is no timezone unless the data index was tz-aware.
- pnl_net = PnL. In v0.6.x, PnL = Size x (Exit - Entry) - commissions.
- commission = Commission (v0.6.5+, MEASURED); gross = PnL + Commission.
- In v0.3.x, commission was baked into the fill prices (EntryPrice/ExitPrice are cost-adjusted), so PnL is net and commission is NOT_MEASURED separately.
- In v0.6.x the 'spread' argument likewise adjusts prices.
- ReturnPct is a FRACTION (0.0158 = 1.58%) despite its name, and it is net of commission.
- Trades still open at the end are excluded, or closed on the last bar, depending on version and settings; say so.
- EntryBar and ExitBar give bar indices, which allow a holding-period check.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
The equity CSV's 'Equity' column is per-bar mark-to-market equity, which is MEASURED and the best source; returns = Equity.pct_change().
If only trades are provided: DECLARED cash (Backtest(cash=...), default 10000) + cumsum(PnL) at ExitTime. This is closed-trade equity only.

formats.platform: vectorbt (open-source, polakowo): Portfolio trades/positions records_readable saved to CSV
formats.export_name: pf.trades.records_readable.to_csv('trades.csv'). pf.trades is ExitTrades by default (settings portfolio.trades_type='exittrades'). Alternatives: pf.entry_trades / pf.exit_trades / pf.positions .records_readable. Equity: pf.value().to_csv('equity.csv').
formats.file_type: csv (pandas default, with a leading unnamed RangeIndex column)
formats.structure:
Verbatim titles from vectorbt/portfolio/trades.py field_config:
- ExitTrades (default): ,Exit Trade Id,Column,Size,Entry Timestamp,Avg Entry Price,Entry Fees,Exit Timestamp,Avg Exit Price,Exit Fees,PnL,Return,Direction,Status,Position Id
- EntryTrades: the first column is 'Entry Trade Id'.
- Positions: the first column is 'Position Id', and there is no parent column.

Values:
- Column is the portfolio column label: a symbol, or a parameter tuple such as (10, 50, 'BTC-USD'). ONE FILE CAN HOLD MANY PARAMETER VARIANTS.
- Size is unsigned.
- Direction is 'Long' or 'Short'.
- Status is 'Open' or 'Closed'.
- Timestamps are the portfolio index values (tz-aware if the data was).
vectorbt PRO uses different titles (e.g. 'Entry Index', 'Exit Index', 'Entry Order Id'); these are UNVERIFIED.
columns: Exit Trade Id | Entry Trade Id | Position Id
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
- Filter Status == 'Closed'. Open rows are valued at the last price.
- side = Direction; qty = Size.
- entry = Entry Timestamp / Avg Entry Price; exit = Exit Timestamp / Avg Exit Price.
- pnl_net = PnL, which vectorbt computes as size x (exit - entry) x (+1 long, -1 short) - Entry Fees - Exit Fees (verified in nb.get_trade_stats_nb).
- commission = Entry Fees + Exit Fees (MEASURED); gross = PnL + fees.
- Return = PnL / (Size x Avg Entry Price), as a fraction.
- Several Exit Trades with the same Position Id are pieces of one position.
- If Column has more than one distinct value, treat the file as a variants matrix. Give each Column its own trade list and feed them to CSCV PBO / DSR with n_trials = number of distinct Columns (MEASURED) instead of the declared count.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
Preferred: pf.value() per bar (MEASURED mark-to-market).
From trades only: DECLARED init_cash (default 100) + cumsum(PnL of Closed trades) by Exit Timestamp, per Column.
formats.encoding_notes:
- If a tuple-valued Column is serialised as a string like "(10, 50, 'BTC-USD')", keep it opaque as a variant key.
- Fees are in quote currency.

formats.platform: backtrader: no native per-trade export; the common user-saved files
formats.export_name:
(a) PyFolio analyzer: cerebro.addanalyzer(bt.analyzers.PyFolio, _name='pyfolio'); returns, positions, transactions, gross_lev = strat.analyzers.pyfolio.get_pf_items(); transactions.to_csv(...); returns.to_csv(...).
(b) bt.analyzers.Transactions (the same fields as a dict).
(c) The community TradeList analyzer (ab-trader/backtrader_addons trade_list, needs Cerebro(tradehistory=True)), dumped with pd.DataFrame(...).to_csv(index=False).
(d) A custom notify_trade CSV with no standard header.
formats.structure:
PyFolio transactions CSV: date,amount,price,sid,symbol,value
- date is a UTC datetime index; amount is signed (+ buy, - sell); value = -amount x price; no commission column.

PyFolio returns CSV: index,return (UTC dates; per-period simple returns).

PyFolio positions CSV: index,<data name>...,cash (value per asset plus cash).

TradeList analyzer CSV: ref,ticker,dir,datein,pricein,dateout,priceout,chng%,pnl,pnl%,size,value,cumpnl,nbars,pnl/bar,mfe,mae,mfe%,mae%
- pnl = trade pnlcomm, so it is NET.
- pnl% = pnl / broker value x 100.
- mfe and mae are PER-UNIT price distances (not currency totals); mfe% and mae% are % of entry price.
- dir is 'long' or 'short'.
- size is signed (the maximum size during the trade).

Custom notify_trade dumps usually take trade.ref, trade.data._name, bt.num2date(trade.dtopen / dtclose), trade.price (average entry), trade.pnl (gross), trade.pnlcomm (net), trade.commission and trade.barlen. Note that trade.size is 0 once the trade is closed.
formats.round_trip_reconstruction:
From PyFolio/Transactions:
1. Sort by date, then FIFO-pair per symbol. A trade opens when the position leaves 0 and closes when it returns to 0 or flips.
2. side = the sign of the opening amount; entry and exit prices are volume-weighted.
3. pnl_gross = sum(-value) over the round trip.
4. Commission is NOT_MEASURED.

From TradeList: one row per trade.
- side = dir; qty = abs(size).
- entry = datein/pricein; exit = dateout/priceout.
- pnl_net = pnl. Commission is not separated (NOT_MEASURED); gross is unknown.

From a custom notify_trade CSV: require a column mapping step (pnl vs pnlcomm) from the client, and tag the result DECLARED.
formats.equity_reconstruction:
PyFolio returns CSV: equity = DECLARED starting cash x cumprod(1 + return). The returns are MEASURED per-period mark-to-market (broker value based), so this is the preferred equity input for PSR/DSR/bootstrap.
The positions CSV row-sum (assets + cash) gives the portfolio value directly.
TradeList: starting cash (DECLARED) + cumpnl.
formats.encoding_notes: backtrader has no canonical trade CSV. Treat backtrader uploads as 'returns series' (PyFolio returns) plus optional FIFO-paired transactions. Show a column-mapping UI for anything else.
